items.h: Eli Raridon Has Deep-League Streaming Appeal with WRs Sidelined
items.s: New England Patriots tight end Eli Raridon may be the No. 2 option on the depth chart behind Hunter Henry, but there's still an opportunity for him to carve out fantasy value in Week 8 against the Miami Dolphins. Raridon has played more than 50% of the snaps in every game he's been healthy for this season, and he has double-digit PPR points in three of his last four contests. In addition to his solid snap share and increased volume lately, Raridon could benefit from a depleted receiver room this week. Raridon and fellow tight end Hunter Henry are both headed for larger roles with A.J. Brown (knee) unlikely to play and Romeo Doubs (shoulder) and Mack Hollins (calf) both on injured reserve.…

items.h: Eli Raridon Worth Adding After Another Strong Performance
items.s: New England Patriots rookie tight end Eli Raridon caught three of four targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Thursday's Week 7 loss to Chicago, including a 30-yard scoring reception from Drake Maye. Raridon also caught five for 57 against Las Vegas in Week 5 and has 12 catches for 168 yards and two touchdowns in six appearances. Hunter Henry remains New England's primary tight end, catching seven passes for 71 yards against Chicago, but Raridon is establishing a receiving role of his own. His big-play ability makes him an intriguing Week 8 pickup against Miami.

items.h: Gets into end zone Thursday
items.s: Raridon caught three of four targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Thursday's Week 7 loss to the Bears. Raridon got open late in the third quarter and hauled in a nicely placed pass from Drake Maye for a 30-yard score. The rookie tight end finished third on the team with 56 receiving yards and tied for third with three receptions. Raridon is clearly behind Hunter Henry, who posted a 7-71-0 receiving line on seven targets, in the tight-end pecking order, but he's shown promise early in his career with 12 catches on 16 targets for 168 yards and two TDs through six games.

items.h: Eli Raridon hits paydirt in Week 7
items.s: Eli Raridon secured 3-of-4 targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Thursday's 30-24 loss to the Bears. Raridon emerged during a five-catch performance back in Week 5. He almost disappeared in Week 6, but the rookie third-rounder stepped back up Thursday night. Raridon scored his second career TD on a 30-yard strike from QB Drake Maye in the third quarter of this one, and he's certainly a talented young player for fantasy managers to keep tabs on.

items.h: Rookie Eli Raridon Still Mostly a Dynasty Stash at Tight End
items.s: New England Patriots rookie third-round tight end Eli Raridon has clear pass-catching potential at the position in just his first year in the league, but Hunter Henry's presence makes him a volatile, touchdown-dependent TE2/3 option every week. The 22-year-old from Notre Dame popped for a five-catch, 57-yard game on Oct. 11 in a blowout win over the Las Vegas Raiders, and he has played nearly 60% of the offensive snaps in each of the last three games. Through his first five NFL games, Raridon has caught nine of his 12 targets for 112 yards and one touchdown, while Henry has 19 receptions for 225 yards and two touchdowns on 24 targets in six games. If anything were to happen to Henry,…

items.h: Eli Raridon's Five-Catch Outing Raises Fantasy Intrigue
items.s: New England Patriots tight end Eli Raridon enjoyed the most productive game of his young career in Sunday's 45-17 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders, catching all five of his targets for 57 yards. The third-round rookie entered Week 5 with just three receptions for 44 yards and a touchdown across his first three appearances, making the increased receiving involvement particularly encouraging. Raridon played 43 offensive snaps (57%) against Las Vegas after logging 44 snaps (58%) in Week 4, indicating that his larger receiving workload came without a significant change in playing time. Veteran Hunter Henry remains New England's primary tight end, playing 48 snaps against the Raiders while…

items.h: Productive in Week 5 victory
items.s: Raridon caught all five of his targets for 57 yards during the Patriots' 45-17 win over the Raiders on Sunday. The rookie third-rounder accumulated three catches (on four targets) for 44 yards and a score in each of his first three games, and he eclipsed those receiving marks (except the score) during Sunday's blowout win. His five catches co-led the Patriots with Efton Chism, and the duo finished tied for the third-most receiving yards behind Kyle Williams (91) and DeMario Douglas (65). Raridon's 43 offensive snaps were only slightly behind top tight end Hunter Henry (48), and the former has played more than 50 percent of New England's offensive snaps in each of the last two weeks. The…

items.h: Eli Raridon hauls in five passes in Week 5 win
items.s: Eli Raridon caught all five of his targets for 57 yards in the Patriots 45-17 win over the Raiders. Raridon set new season highs in receptions, targets, and receiving yards in the win over Las Vegas. The rookie continues to see Hunter Henry see the bulk of the snaps, but Raridon is carving out a role after the first five weeks of the season.

items.h: Not listed on injury report
items.s: Raridon (ankle) was not listed in Wednesday's injury report ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders. Raridon exited Sunday's win over the Bills due to an ankle injury. However, he's not listed on the injury report ahead of the Week 5 meeting with Las Vegas.

items.h: Questionable to return Sunday
items.s: Raridon (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against Buffalo. Raridon didn't play in Week 3 against the Jaguars due to a hamstring injury. However, an ankle injury could mean he won't be back in Week 4. If Raridon can't return, Cameron Latu could see more work behind Hunter Henry.

items.h: Back in action in Week 4
items.s: Raridon (thigh) is listed as active Sunday at Buffalo. After missing Week 3 due to a thigh injury, Raridon was limited on all three Week 4 practice reports and then listed as questionable for Sunday's contest. Now that the rookie third-rounder is confirmed to be available, he'll hop back in as the No. 2 TE behind Hunter Henry, which so far has equated to a 2-32-1 line on two targets through the first two games of his career.

items.h: Raridon (thigh) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bills, Phil Perry of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.s: Raridon was a limited participant in all three practices during Week 4 prep, which was enough for the rookie third-rounder to draw the questionable tag for Sunday's AFC East showdown. If Raridon is cleared to play, then he would slot behind Hunter Henry on the tight end depth chart ahead of Cameron Latu and Tanner Arkin.

items.h: Raridon (thigh) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
items.s: Raridon has now opened Week 4 prep with consecutive limited practices. If the thigh injury keeps Raridon off the field for Sunday's game against the Bills, Tanner Arkin could see more snaps behind Hunter Henry and Cameron Latu.

items.h: Raridon (thigh) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
items.s: A thigh injury prevented the rookie third-rounder from playing against the Jaguars in Week 3. He was limited in all three practices prior to New England's loss to Jacksonville, so he may have to log a full practice over the next two days to have a realistic chance of playing Sunday against Buffalo.

items.h: Raridon (thigh) is listed as inactive Week 3 against the Jaguars.
items.s: Raridon saw the field for 36 snaps in Week 1, but his Week 2 showing was cut short due to his thigh injury. After sitting out practice Thursday and Friday, the rookie will ultimately miss his first career game, paving the way for Cameron Latu and Tanner Arkin to work in a reserve capacity behind starting tight end Hunter Henry.

items.h: Raridon (thigh) is listed as questionable ahead of Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
items.s: Raridon started the week as a limited participant Wednesday before downgrading to a non-participant in Thursday and Friday's practice sessions. The rookie third-rounder has still managed to draw the questionable tag despite consecutive absences, meaning Raridon's absences the last two days may have been at least partly for rest/precautionary reasons.

items.h: Raridon (thigh) did not practice Thursday.
items.s: Raridon was injured in Sunday's 20-3 win over the Steelers, but he was able to practice in a limited capacity Wednesday. However, the 22-year-old appeared to take a step back by missing Thursday's session. Raridon will have another opportunity to practice Friday or else he may carry an injury designation ahead of the Week 3 meeting with Jacksonville on Sunday. The rookie appeared in both of the Patriots' games to begin the 2026 campaign, catching both targets for 32 yards and one touchdown.

items.h: Raridon (thigh) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday.
items.s: Raridon was forced to leave Sunday's 20-3 win over the Steelers in the first half with a thigh injury, and he was unable to return to the game. The tight end's ability to practice in any capacity Wednesday is a positive sign, and he'll have two more chances to log a full practice before the team faces the Jaguars in Week 3.

items.h: Raridon (thigh) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Steelers.
items.s: Raridon exited the game after hauling in a 30-yard pass from Drake Maye. The catch that caused the tight end to enter the medical tent was his only target in the contest.

items.h: Raridon is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Steelers due to a thigh injury.
items.s: Raridon hauled in a 30-yard pass from Drake Maye before going to the blue medical tent to be evaluated for a thigh injury. Cameron Latu will serve as the backup tight end behind Hunter Henry for as long as Raridon is sidelined.

items.h: Raridon caught his only target for a two-yard touchdown in Wednesday's 13-10 loss to the Seahawks.
items.s: Raridon opened the scoring in the second quarter with a two-yard touchdown catch on his first career target, but the Patriots failed to hold onto the lead. The rookie third-round pick out of Notre Dame played 38 of the team's 71 snaps on offense, and Raridon is the clear No. 2 tight end behind Hunter Henry, who caught all three of his targets Wednesday.

items.h: Raridon will enter training camp with an opportunity to establish himself as the No. 2 tight end behind starter Hunter Henry, Jordy McElroy of USA Today reports.
items.s: The Patriots selected Raridon in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft, and he has a clear path to snaps with Julian Hill (knee) on season-ending IR and Austin Hooper having signed with the Falcons. At 6-foot-6, 245 pounds, the Notre Dame standout possesses the athleticism, speed and catch radius to threaten defenses down the seam and provide Drake Maye with another receiving option. Raridon still needs refinement as a blocker, but a strong training camp could position him for a meaningful rookie-year role. Meanwhile, Henry is positioned to hit free agency in 2027.

items.h: New England selected Raridon in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft, 95th overall.
items.s: Raridon spent his entire four-year college career with Notre Dame, and he was able to overcome knee injuries in 2022 and 2023 to become a productive starter for the Fighting Irish. He put it all together in 2025 with 32 catches for 482 yards over 12 games, though he did not haul in a touchdown pass. Raridon showed steady improvement as a pass catcher over the course of his college career and has the athletic foundation (6-foot-6, 245 pounds) to establish himself as a large target in the passing game for Drake Maye, though the former will need to work on his blocking ability in order to earn…
